domains.domain: CRM contacts — list, person detail, mobile fork
domains.headline: The contacts domain is a faithful FUB clone built as TWO separate products — a dense desktop tree and a thin mobile tree, both server-rendered on every request and toggled by a CSS breakpoint — sitting on an uncached query storm (~85 Supabase round-trips per list view from per-view/per-stage/per-sequence COUNT fan-outs; ~40-55 queries across four sequential await-stages per person view). Its most critical user-facing failures cluster on the send path: both composers submit multi-second server actions with no pending state, no double-send protection, and no state reset (the sent text stays in the box), and on mobile the conversation feed snapshots server props into state so a sent message never appears in the thread — together making duplicate texts to clients the natural outcome of normal use. Five of seven mobile mutation wrappers swallow errors entirely, the same concept (market reports, saved searches, automations, CMA/BPO) is editable in 3-5 competing widgets on one page, and the capability matrix forces device-hopping (rename a contact: phone only; log a call or send a CMA: desktop only; bulk actions: desktop only; desktop list has no search box while its Text/Call icons bypass the compliance-gated Twilio path with raw sms:/tel: links). RBAC, the AST query compiler, the bulk-job framework, and the SMS compliance chain are genuinely solid and worth carrying into the rebuild.

domains.domain: Messaging — inbox, SMS, email, group messages, delivery visibility
domains.headline: The messaging server core is compliance-hardened and largely correct (suppression chokepoint, A2P fail-closed, signed webhooks, forward-only delivery state), but the UI around it is why the owner suffers: sends are plain form-actions that serially await Twilio plus ~10 DB reads plus a full force-dynamic re-render of a page that rescans 2,000 timeline rows, with zero pending state, no idempotency key, and a controlled textarea that keeps the sent text after the redirect — so sends feel hung and double-taps produce real duplicate texts; group messages are faithfully recorded in payload JSON that no UI component reads, so a group text is pixel-identical to a 1:1 everywhere, and replying from the inbox silently drops every other group participant; delivery state is written to the DB by webhook but rendered on exactly one surface (desktop person-detail), never in the inbox; and the same conversation is rendered by four different components with four different capability sets across desktop and mobile.

criticalDefects.userImpact: Owner taps Send, sees nothing change for 2-6s while Twilio + ~10 serial DB reads + a full page re-render run, sees his text still in the box with a live Send button, taps again, and the client receives duplicate texts.
criticalDefects.rootCause: Form-action + redirect as the only update mechanism; controlled composer state not reset by navigation; no client send state machine and no server idempotency key.

Only media suppression, listing_photos curation, resort-community flags, photo curation, and the media library are wired end-to-end to real outcomes. The 2026-07-07 consolidation cleaned up the duplicate top-level routes into redirects, but left /admin/guides orphaned from nav, 378 lines of dead sync components, an optimization page whose cron is never scheduled, and a sync cockpit that polls every 5 seconds forever in engineer jargon a broker cannot use.

domains.headline: The admin is slow because every page is force-dynamic with all UI state in searchParams and every render fans out to dozens of live, uncached Supabase queries: /admin/crm executes ~90 queries per render (40 live count(*) for saved-view badges + 35 sequence-status head-counts consumed only as dropdown options + 8 stage counts + exact counts over the 22,865-row crm_people table), /admin/crm/inbox re-downloads a 2,000-row joined message window carrying ~1.4 MB of bodies on every folder switch, thread open, and post-triage router.refresh(), and /admin/crm/[id] runs 45-55 queries across up to 7 sequential stages — then every mutation calls router.refresh(), re-running the entire fan-out to show one tag. There is no Suspense streaming on any hot page (3 loading.tsx + 32 Suspense across 150 pages), zero next/dynamic code-splitting under 53,250 lines of 'use client' admin code, every CRM route server-renders and ships BOTH the mobile and desktop trees, and every admin page also downloads the public site's chrome/tracking bundle (SiteHeader, VisitTracker, GTM, InstallPrompt) that no-ops at runtime via usePathname.

domains.domain: Consumer-side account (saved homes, saved searches, account hub, auth funnel, alert delivery)
domains.headline: The /account pages themselves are the cleanest consumer code in the repo, but the system around them is severed at every seam: a signed-in user has no way to reach their account from the site chrome (the header always says "Sign in" — the account menu component has zero importers), the save-a-home → sign-in → resume funnel is broken in all three of its variants (nothing consumes the return params and the intended save never happens), Viewing History reads a table (user_activities) that nothing in the entire codebase writes, password sign-in skips the guest-alert claim that OAuth gets (so email subscribers see an empty saved-searches page while still receiving alerts), and interest in a home is scattered across seven parallel persistence systems (saved_listings, likes, saved_cities, saved_communities, community_likes, listing_collections, listing_alerts + zombie saved_searches) with inconsistent key canonicalization. The one healthy spine is the unified listing_alerts pipeline — guest/signed-in/broker rows in one table, a careful hourly send cron with seen-set diffing and compliance gates, and the broker CRM reading the same table — which the rebuild should treat as the model; meanwhile saved homes, the strongest buyer signal collected, never reaches the broker UI at all.

domains.domain: API + server-action surface (186 app/api route files / 199 method handlers, 161 app/actions files / 664 exported functions)
domains.headline: The surface is enormous (199 HTTP handlers + 664 server actions) and only partly consolidated. A canonical guard module exists (lib/auth/guards.ts) but adoption is incomplete: routes authenticate through ~8 distinct mechanisms and — most importantly — the primary admin mutation surface (server actions) carries no in-body auth, relying entirely on the (protected) layout that only gates page rendering, not the action POST. Layered on top are ~24 genuinely dead routes, 7 dead action files, several duplicate-capability clusters (unified vs per-platform social publish, weekly-cycle aliases, sync-route sprawl, uncentralized email/SMS senders), 13 orphaned crons not on any schedule, and an internal HTTP self-fetch fan-out anti-pattern. The rebuild needs one auth entry point, self-authorizing actions, de-duplicated send/publish/sync paths, and a cron reconciliation against vercel.json.
